aqueducts.name: Acueducto Chapala–Guadalajara
aqueducts.capacity_note: Design 7.5 m3/s; concession 240 hm3/yr = 7.61 m3/s; pumping station (6×1.5 m3/s KSB pumps, 138 m head) cannot deliver design flow; actual Chapala extraction 6.65 m3/s in 2025 (incl. Sistema Antiguo).
aqueducts.description: Pumping station on the north shore of Lake Chapala (km 0, 1526 m) → 26 km rising main to Caja Cambio de Régimen (km 25.9, 1608 m) → gravity to Tanque de Entrega Cerro del Cuatro (km 42.3) → Caja Enlace → PP1 Miravalle (km 48.1); also feeds PP2 Las Huertas.
aqueducts.route_note: Schematic only: straight segments between known endpoints (OSM-mapped pumping station, Cerro del Cuatro summit from OSM/Nominatim, PP1). The real alignment (incl. the km-26 regime-change tank) is not published as coordinates.

aqueducts.name: Sistema Antiguo Chapala–Guadalajara (Río Santiago – Canal de Atequiza – Presa Las Pintas)
aqueducts.capacity_note: Open-channel system; share ~20% of AMG supply (PIA an-0011). Chainage 0+000 Ocotlán → 39+000 Presa Corona → 67+332 PB1 → 93+000 PB2 → 97+568 PP1 Miravalle.
aqueducts.description: Lake water enters Río Santiago at Ocotlán (Planta de Bombeo Ocotlán), flows to Presa derivadora Corona (Poncitlán), then Canal de Atequiza → Presa La Calera / Canal Las Pintas → PB1/PB2 → PP1 Miravalle.
aqueducts.route_note: Ocotlán and Poncitlán are town centroids (Nominatim) standing in for the Ocotlán pumping plant and Presa Corona (river segment drawn straight). The middle section is real OSM canal geometry chained from ways w1436987141, w1436987142, w255993116, w1438774776, w1438774775, w185120559, w185120569, w185120560, w173392591, w1531159458, w1531159457, w1531159456, w1531159462, w1531159461, w1414713595, w1414713594, w173392590, w170809683, w891780832, w891825383, w891825384, w891780831, w891780834, w905665286, w905665287, w170809682, w167412659 (Canal de Atequiza → La Calera area → "Canal Las Pintas"), simplified (Douglas–Peucker ~40 m), with 2 short unmapped gaps (<1.2 km) bridged by straight lines; drawn length ≈89 km vs official 97.6 km; identification of these canals as the Sistema Antiguo is inferred from route and names. Final hop to PP1 is straight.

aqueducts.name: Acueducto Calderón–San Gaspar
aqueducts.capacity_note: Presa Calderón planned for 2 m3/s in bloc (PIA an-0029); CBA an-0007b gives nominal design 1.5 m3/s and historic mean ~0.94–1.01 m3/s; 1.90 m3/s delivered in 2025.
aqueducts.description: Gravity line from Presa Calderón (Acatic/Zapotlanejo) to PP3 San Gaspar, crossing the Río Santiago.
aqueducts.route_note: Straight line between dam wall (OSM) and PP3 (OSM); real alignment not published.

aqueducts.name: Acueducto El Salto–La Red–Calderón
aqueducts.capacity_note: Design 3 m3/s (initially 1 m3/s); pumping plant at Presa El Salto; 54-inch pipe.
aqueducts.description: Pumps Río Verde water (incl. El Zapotillo releases) from Presa El Salto (Valle de Guadalupe) to Presa La Red, which spills down the Río Calderón to Presa Calderón.
aqueducts.route_note: El Salto end uses Valle de Guadalupe town centroid (dam not identifiable in OSM); La Red and Calderón ends are OSM dam walls. La Red→Calderón leg is the Río Calderón (~12 km), not pipe.

aqueducts.name: El Zapotillo – El Salto conduction (Sistema Río Verde → Guadalajara)
aqueducts.capacity_note: Zapotillo–El Salto leg nominally 2 m3/s (Conagua via Crónica 2026); whole Zapotillo–El Salto–La Red–Calderón system: 66 km of aqueducts, 2 pumping plants, +3 m3/s to AMG from 2024, total availability 5 m3/s with Calderón (PIA an-0029). Conagua 2021: 80 m curtain, 3.5 m3/s for AMG.
aqueducts.route_note: Straight schematic; Zapotillo end is an unnamed OSM dam way adjacent to Ejido El Zapotillo (identification inferred).

aqueducts.name: Acueducto Sustituto Chapala–Guadalajara
aqueducts.description: 26 km rising main + 16 km gravity line, new pumping station, surge and regime-change tanks; replaces 1991 line without increasing the 7.5 m3/s concession.
aqueducts.route_note: Schematic, same endpoints as existing aqueduct.

No point-level coordinates are published.

extraction_for_guadalajara.note: Chapala volumes include both the 1991 aqueduct and the Sistema Antiguo (Ocotlán–Atequiza–Las Pintas). Older studies (2008): mean ~5.0 m3/s; 5.96 m3/s in 1998; 4.71 m3/s in 2004.

chapala.role: Lake Chapala is the main source for the Guadalajara metro (≈60% of SIAPA supply; PIA documents say the aqueduct serves >60% of the population). Its level falls ~0.7–1.5 m each dry season (evaporation + extraction) and recovers in the rainy season with Lerma inflows; lows in 1955, 1990–91 and 2001–02 drove the 1991 aqueduct and the search for the Calderón/Zapotillo sources. It is also a Ramsar wetland (site 1973).
